title: parakletos
summary: John 14:15–26 is the direct setting for Jesus’ promise of the Advocate: the Spirit will remain with the disciples and teach and remind them. Ezekiel 36 promises God’s Spirit in a renewed people; Acts 2 narrates the Spirit coming at Pentecost; Romans 8 describes life in the Spirit and adoption. These passages illuminate related aspects of the Spirit’s work, but John’s promise has its own setting and should not be replaced by a general summary of every Spirit passage.
historical_context: The references include a prophetic promise, Jesus’ farewell teaching, the Pentecost narrative, and Paul’s argument about life in the Spirit. The source list supports these textual contexts but does not provide a lexicon or a history of the title used in John.
canonical_context: John 14 promises the Spirit in relation to Jesus’ departure and the disciples’ future teaching and remembrance. Ezekiel and Acts contribute different portrayals of renewal and communal reception; Romans discusses life and adoption. These texts connect within a wider account of the Spirit without making every passage a use of John’s title.
literary_context: Ezekiel speaks prophetically, John records farewell instruction, Acts narrates an event, and Romans develops an argument. John’s promise addresses the disciples before Jesus’ departure; Acts presents a narrated arrival; Romans explains life in the Spirit. The literary settings clarify why their emphases differ.
covenantal_significance: John presents the Spirit as continuing presence and teacher for Jesus’ disciples. Ezekiel connects the Spirit with a renewed heart, Acts with the gathered community, and Romans with life and adoption. The passages show related work while retaining distinct promises and claims.
canonical_role: This entry focuses on Jesus’ promise of the Advocate in John 14 and places it alongside other passages about the Spirit. It distinguishes John’s specific teaching setting from the broader canonical theme.

interpretive_notes.note: Do not reduce parakletos to a single English gloss.
